hypothesis: daemon.boot spawn_to_accept is dominated by supervisor startup work sitting before the socket bind. Profiled (temporary eprintln instrumentation, 8 boots): the supervisor-config atomic write (write_file_atomic -> fsync) inside Supervisor::new was ~31ms p50 (30.9-103.6ms range) of a 31-104ms Supervisor::new, while every other pre-bind phase was <3ms (main_impl settings 0.3ms, telemetry 0.2ms, models/plugins keep-warm spawns 1.1ms, prepare+bind 0.1ms). The file is diagnostic state with no serving-path reader (load_supervisor_config has zero callers; descriptor sweeps skip it by extension), but moving the write after bind was later REJECTED: connect() succeeds before usable hello, and failure mode changes.
approach: SUPERSEDED / REVERTED, not current lane mechanism: crates/pa-daemon/src/supervisor.rs: removed persist_supervisor_config from Supervisor::new; added Supervisor::persist_startup_config called in Supervisor::run immediately after socket bind+restrict+log, before the boot reap and the accept loop. Same payload, same atomic write (write_file_atomic with fsync), same hard-fail-on-error boot contract. Plus an e2e assertion (tests/fd_lifecycle_e2e.rs::booted_supervisor_persists_its_config) that a client which has seen daemon_hello finds a valid supervisor-config (version 1, this socket, resolved default session dir, no lingering temp file). Lane: bd20c604d (perf) + 4d6e80aec/4f75cd055 (test+fix) + e4606e6b2 (fmt) with append-only folds to rust heads f2c02ade, 486457b8, fb5a83de, d3763dca; would-be PR head 54f5e5399; no PR opened.
parity_notes: REJECTED by adversarial review: bind-before-persist exposes a connect-success-but-not-serving window and changes failure semantics; do not treat this paragraph as an accepted parity claim. Historical description: Same socket path/identity, same wire protocol, same features. The supervisor-config file: TS writes it pre-listen too (daemon-supervisor.ts:869 in start()) and TS READS it at construction (:839 via loadPersistedSupervisorConfig :1712, merging the predecessor defaultSessionConfig; deleted at terminal stop :7560). The Rust port never ported that consumer: the Rust payload is default_session_dir, load_supervisor_config has zero callers, and both descriptor sweeps (load_descriptors, find_all_tracked_workers) skip the file by extension. No Rust serving path reads the file; the write still happens exactly once per boot before any client is served. OBSERVABLE FAILURE-MODE CHANGE (adversarially rejected before any PR): a supervisor-config persist failure now occurs with the socket already bound - the process dies holding the bound socket path, and the next boot self-heals via prepare_socket_path's stale-socket cleanup (probe+unlink); before, the socket never appeared. No capability removed: same write, same durability (fsync), same boot-fail-on-error. spawn_to_hello unchanged in total (the fsync moves from before bind to between bind and the accept loop): measured hello p50 b=10.9 vs c=8.4ms (same disk state, poll-tick noise).

daemon.boot.protocol: same-VM ABBA b,c,c,b,b,c on ONE 16-core sandbox VM; daemon.boot isolated (no interleaved suites); pinned binary page-warmed (cat > /dev/null) identically before each arm; sha-asserted pins (versions.json per run); 30/30 trials valid (accept/hello/create true, err none). Both arms share the same 5.4-5.6ms warm exec floor; the base arm shows fsync-flush bursts (20.8-88.0ms on 6/15 trials) the candidate arm lacks (max 25.9ms scheduler-tick noise). The disk is bimodal: on slow-flush states (persist profiled 30.9-103.6ms; f2c02ade cross-VM base warm trials 91.6-892.0ms) the gain is far larger; not evidence of a usable-latency improvement for this post-bind candidate.

validity.notes: Historical post-bind pair only; NO PR was opened for this implementation. The pair does not measure the later pivot. PR pair: 30/30 daemon.boot trials valid; noop harness floor ~0.05-0.09ms. Void-pair disclosure: an earlier ABBA attempt pinned BOTH arms to the candidate (bins-b vs bins-base path bug; versions.json caught it) - excluded as evidence, kept as a candidate A/A that characterized cold-exec noise. Cross-VM pairs kept only as corroboration per the fleet methodology addendum (VM factor: cand-VM cold_start ~2900ms vs base-VM ~750ms at one hour). This arm only advances connect() readiness, while daemon_hello still waits for config persistence; this pair cannot support a usable-latency win. Fleet baseline caveat: the 76.5ms fleet spawn_to_accept baseline is a warm/cold mixture; the warm-floor comparison here (10.6 -> 5.6ms p50 on identical warm cache state) is the apples-to-apples claim. Disk: Prime sandbox VM network-backed storage with bimodal fsync latency (2-5ms fast path, e.g. base pr4-b all-5.5ms trials, vs 30-104ms+ flushes) - numbers are for THIS disk class, not a local-SSD claim.

decision: NO PR opened for this post-bind mechanism. Rejected during adversarial pre-review: connect() success can precede usable daemon_hello, and bind-before-persist changes failure semantics. Reverted by pivot commit 5114b3893; measured figures remain as historical mechanism evidence only, not evidence for the pivot or a merge recommendation.
